topics: Gossip about the town guards: so many are retired adventurers who 'took an arrow to the knee'. Who is stingy, who cries when drunk, who tells tales to the captain.

Dibella's faith and where the line falls: the priestesses at Dibella's temple in Markarth hate being called whores, while Haelga in Riften uses the faith as an excuse to do as she pleases. Where does worship end and the trade begin?

The civil war and how the customers have changed: Stormcloaks against Imperials, compared by how fat their purses are, how loose their tongues and how rough their hands. The golden rule of the trade is never to say which side you are on.
Skooma and the girls who vanished: a fellow worker who got hooked on skooma and disappeared, and how to deal with the Khajiit caravan traders.

Keeping the Thieves Guild at arm's length: in Riften no one crosses the Guild or the Black-Briar family. Offers of a side job going through customers' pockets; refuse and there is trouble, accept and there is trouble too.
The Temple of Mara and marriage: wear an Amulet of Mara and you can marry. A former colleague who quit the trade and married; some envy her, some sneer.
Dangerous customers: vampires, werewolves, a man with strange tattoos. Should they report them to the Vigilants of Stendarr, or stay out of it?
Joking about cursing a customer who treated a girl badly with the Black Sacrament; maybe only half joking. The business with young Aventus Aretino in Windhelm is going around too.
Race, and who looks down on whom: the Dunmer of Windhelm's Gray Quarter, the Argonian dockworkers, Nord prejudice. Even among the girls, where you come from decides your place.
Sanguine's revels: a customer swore he had the night of his life, woke up in another city and had apparently stolen a goat. Maybe a Daedric Prince's prank.
Dreams of retiring: what they would do with their savings. Open an inn, make the pilgrimage to High Hrothgar, go home to Cyrodiil. They know it won't happen, but they talk about it anyway.
The Bards College and its songs: complaints about the bawdy tavern songs written about them, scorn for the songs that make them sound prettier than they are, and grumbling that poets are bad payers.
examples: He was going on about his knee again. That's the third time.
Dibella preaches love, but she doesn't pay the rent.
The ones in blue always pay. The ones in furs tip well, but what a mouth on them.
I hadn't seen her in ages, then someone said they spotted her down in the Ratway...
Maven's man came by again. Says he wants 'information'.
She married a farmer, you know. Cabbage fields every day? ...Still, I'm a little jealous.
I've made a rule: no customers who want to bite my neck. I'm not joking.
All you need is human bones and a heart, right? ...Maybe I'll ask the butcher.
Nord customers say 'no ash-skins', but once they're drunk anyone will do.
This Sanguine, shouldn't we make him our patron?
Someday I'll run a little tailor's shop in Solitude. ...In twenty years or so.
Poets try to pay you with a song. You can't buy bread with a song.
